title: Breast cancer early detection - is it feasible to use breast milk as a liquid biopsy to detect breast cancer?
official: Breast cancer early detection - breast milk (BRACELET-BM1): a feasibility study
summary:
Background and study aims
Pregnancy related breast cancer (PRBC) is breast cancer diagnosed during pregnancy and postpartum breast cancer (PPBC) is breast cancer diagnosed within ten years after having a baby. Both PRBC and PPBC are associated with poor survival outcomes. Early detection of PRBC/PPBC in very high risk women is difficult and relies on cessation of breastfeeding to resume mammographic screening, despite continued breastfeeding lowering breast cancer risk.

This study is intended to investigate whether breast milk samples could be used in the future to detect early breast cancer, particularly in women high-risk for breast cancer. To do this we need to establish the best way to collect, transport and test breast milk in the laboratory. We are also investigating how acceptable this research is to the women who are involved.

Who can participate?
Women who are breastfeeding/expressing breast milk and at least 14 days postpartum.

What does the study involve?
Participants will provide a breast milk sample (aiming for 20ml per breast) and a blood sample (approximately 10ml).
Baseline data collection will include age, previous breast cancer history and pathology details (if applicable), age of baby, number of previous children, any breast abnormalities noticed and details of related referrals, comorbidities and confirmation of BC risk using Tyrer-Cuzick model.
Particiants will complete a brief questionnaire and structured interview which will be audio recorded.
Five participants will be offered a repeat study visit to repeat milk and blood samples collection and questionnaire/interview 8 weeks later.
Follow up will be for ten years, checking participant NHS number against a national cancer registry.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
This study hopes to provide pilot data for further research using this innovative non-invasive method and establish the first protocol for breast milk as a liquid biopsy.

Risks to participants include:
Potential discomfort/bleeding from the blood test.
Possibility of psychological distress and cancer-related anxiety related to being investigated for cancer despite being well and not being high risk for breast cancer or possibly being informed of a higher lifetime risk of breast cancer than expected. We will monitor for any psychological impact during our structured interviews at each appointment, and advice will be given on reducing breast cancer risk in the future with lifestyle interventions.
Very low possibility that samples given may seem suspicious for cancer. If this happens contact will be made to discuss further and if necessary a referral will be made for further investigations including examination and potentially a breast scan and biopsy. This process may cause anxiety and distress.

Where is the study run from?
Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
June 2026 to June 2037.

Who is funding the study?
1. The Academy of Medical Sciences Starter Grant
2. Prevent Breast Cancer 
3. Paterson Project Awards from The Christie 2030 Research Programme

Who is the main contact? 
Nicola Flaum, nicola.flaum@manchester.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Women breastfeeding/expressing breast milk
2.	≥14 days postpartum
3.	General-population level BC risk, very high risk (VHR) for BC or with a history or diagnosis of breast cancer
Exclusion criteria:
1. Refusal or inability to give informed consent
2. Any acute or chronic condition that would limit the ability of the participant to take part in the study
